patient.chief_complaint: Sudden onset severe headache 3 hours ago, brief unconsciousness, on anticoagulation
patient.history_present_illness: Mr. Sullivan is a 62-year-old male with atrial fibrillation on apixaban who presents with sudden onset severe headache 3 hours ago. He was sitting in his living room watching television when he experienced an abrupt onset of an extremely severe headache, rated 10/10, accompanied by immediate nausea and vomiting. His wife noted he briefly lost responsiveness for approximately 45 seconds and became unresponsive. He regained consciousness spontaneously. He was brought to the emergency department by ambulance. He is now alert but continues to complain of severe headache with neck stiffness. He is on apixaban 5 mg twice daily for atrial fibrillation and took his last dose this morning at 8 AM, approximately 6 hours before presentation. He notes he takes his medications reliably. His anticoagulation status is an important complicating factor. The neurovascular team is concerned about the interaction between anticoagulation and both the hemorrhage severity and potential endovascular intervention. His blood pressure in the ED is extremely elevated. He denies any prior history of severe headaches or similar events.

results.finding: After SAH, anticoagulation for afib should be delayed minimum 4 weeks; typically 4-8 weeks post-securing of aneurysm
Risk of cardioembolic stroke from afib must be balanced against rebleeding risk
DOAC restart preferred over warfarin when resuming anticoagulation post-SAH

output.summary: After SAH, anticoagulation should be held for at least 4 weeks post-aneurysm treatment. Restart timing depends on hemorrhage control, neurological stability, and CHA2DS2-VASc score. Apixaban or rivaroxaban preferred over warfarin when restarting. This patient with atrial fibrillation and SAH requires coordinated neurology/cardiology management for anticoagulation timing.

key_reasoning_points: Factor Xa inhibitors (apixaban) do not affect INR - anti-Xa level is needed to assess anticoagulation
Andexanet alfa is the specific reversal agent for apixaban/rivaroxaban; 4F-PCC is alternative
Timing of last apixaban dose (6 hours ago) determines protocol: high-dose reversal required
Basilar apex aneurysm location is associated with higher surgical risk - endovascular coiling preferred
Fisher grade 4 SAH (extensive blood + IVH) carries highest vasospasm and DCI risk
Severe Takotsubo cardiomyopathy (EF 35%) limits ability to use triple-H therapy for vasospasm
